questions.text: What mechanism is PostgreSQL physical replication based on?

answers.text: Transmitting WAL records to a standby and applying them there
Periodically running pg_dump for every table
Transmitting only SQL INSERT commands
Copying only the system catalog

questions.explanation: Physical replication transfers changes through WAL, and the standby server applies the received log records.

questions.text: Which statements about PostgreSQL physical replication are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: It creates an exact copy of the entire cluster
It is one-way
It requires binary compatibility between servers
It allows individual tables to be selected independently for replication

questions.explanation: The summary describes physical replication as a one-way mechanism that creates an exact copy of the entire cluster and requires binary compatibility.

questions.text: What is a standby server for physical replication initially created from?

answers.text: A physical backup of the primary server
An empty initdb cluster without copying data
Only a pg_dumpall SQL script
Only an archive of configuration files

questions.explanation: The lesson starts building a standby from a physical copy of the primary server; the standby then continues receiving and applying new WAL.

source.locator: Creating a standby from a physical backup

questions.text: Which processes participate in streaming physical replication? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: wal sender on the primary server
wal receiver on the standby
startup on the standby
autovacuum launcher as the WAL transmitter

questions.explanation: In the lesson scheme, wal sender transmits the WAL stream, wal receiver receives it, and the changes are applied on the standby during recovery.

source.locator: Primary, wal sender, wal receiver, startup scheme

questions.text: Which standby process connects to the primary server's wal sender during streaming replication?

answers.text: wal receiver
checkpointer
autovacuum worker
logger

questions.explanation: In streaming mode, the standby wal receiver connects to the primary wal sender through the replication protocol.

questions.text: Which statements about streaming replication are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: The standby receives a stream of WAL records through the replication protocol
It can minimize replication lag
With the appropriate synchronous configuration, commit can wait for confirmation from a standby
Transmission starts only after each WAL segment is completely filled

questions.explanation: Unlike a file archive, streaming replication transmits WAL records directly through a replication connection.

questions.text: Why does file-based replication usually lag further behind the primary than streaming replication?

answers.text: The archive is updated only after a WAL segment switch
File-based replication does not use WAL
The standby applies only every second segment
The archive transmits only DDL commands

questions.explanation: A file archive receives completed WAL segments, so an additional delay occurs between segment arrivals.

questions.text: Which statements about file-based and streaming replication are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: File-based replication is possible when continuous WAL archiving is configured
File-based replication usually has higher lag
In practice, a file archive can supplement streaming replication
Streaming and file-based replication fundamentally cannot be used together

questions.explanation: The material recommends treating the WAL archive as an additional WAL source for a streaming standby.

questions.text: Which parameter determines how much information is written to WAL in the context of enabling physical replication?

answers.text: wal_level
hot_standby_feedback
max_connections
work_mem

questions.explanation: wal_level controls the contents of WAL. For replication, the log must contain all information required about changes.

questions.text: What is true for wal_level = replica as presented? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: The level contains information required for physical replication
It allows hot physical backups to be used
According to the material, it is the default level in PostgreSQL 10 and later
It is intended only for crash recovery and does not support replication

questions.explanation: The notes contrast the old minimal level with replica: replica contains the data required for hot backup and physical replication.

questions.text: What does synchronous physical replication add to the wait during transaction commit in the scheme discussed?

answers.text: Waiting for confirmation that the synchronous standby received the WAL records
Waiting for a SELECT to complete on the standby
Waiting for a complete logical database dump
Waiting for automatic switching of master and replica roles

questions.explanation: Synchronous mode increases durability at the cost of additional waiting during COMMIT.

questions.text: What are the consequences of synchronous replication mode? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Durability of committed data is increased
COMMIT can take longer because it waits for the standby
synchronous_standby_names is used to select the synchronous standby
Any reads from different servers automatically receive one shared consistent snapshot

questions.explanation: Synchronization concerns commit acknowledgment; it does not create a common consistent snapshot for arbitrary simultaneous reads from different servers.

questions.text: What is a client allowed to do on a standby in hot standby mode?

answers.text: Connect and execute read-only queries
Execute arbitrary INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE statements
Create permanent and temporary tables
Run VACUUM and REINDEX

questions.explanation: Hot standby allows read queries while WAL is being applied, but operations that modify data are prohibited.

questions.text: Which actions are unavailable on a standby in hot standby mode? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: DDL commands that change object structure
SELECT FOR UPDATE and other locks that imply modification
VACUUM, ANALYZE, and REINDEX
An ordinary SELECT that does not modify data

questions.explanation: Reading is allowed on a hot standby, but actions that directly or indirectly modify database state are prohibited.

questions.text: What happens to client connections to a standby server if hot_standby = off is set?

answers.text: Connections are unavailable during recovery
Write operations become allowed
The standby automatically becomes the primary server
WAL application stops

questions.explanation: The notes call this a warm standby: recovery continues, but client connections to the standby are not allowed.

questions.text: Which situations can cause a conflict between a read query on a hot standby and WAL application? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: The standby needs to apply a change that is incompatible with the running query
The primary removes row versions that are still required by a query on the standby
WAL application cannot wait indefinitely for every read query
Any SELECT always and automatically blocks WAL application forever

questions.explanation: A hot standby serves read queries while applying changes from the primary, so conflicts can arise between these activities.

questions.text: Which parameter controls the allowed delay when applying conflicting WAL records on a standby?

answers.text: max_standby_streaming_delay
synchronous_standby_names
wal_level
archive_command

questions.explanation: The exercise directly associates max_standby_streaming_delay with delaying the application of conflicting records on the standby server.

questions.text: Which statements about hot_standby_feedback are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: The parameter enables feedback from the standby to the primary server
It helps prevent the primary from removing row versions still required by standby queries
Using it can allow a long-running query on the standby to avoid cancellation caused by cleanup on the primary
It switches the standby into write mode

questions.explanation: The exercise demonstrates feedback: when it is enabled, cleanup on the primary can be delayed for queries running on the standby.

questions.text: Why connect several physical standbys in a cascade?

answers.text: To reduce load on the primary server and redistribute network traffic
To allow writes on all standbys at the same time
To eliminate WAL
So each standby contains only one database

questions.explanation: With cascading, some standbys receive WAL from another standby rather than directly from the primary, reducing load on the source node and nearby network.

questions.text: Which tasks can PostgreSQL physical replication solve? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Increasing data durability
Using a standby server for read workloads
Reducing load on the primary with multiple or cascading standbys
Independently modifying different rows of one cluster in both directions on all servers

questions.explanation: Replication is presented as a basic mechanism for improving durability and distributing read and network load, while remaining one-way physical replication.

source.locator: High Availability, Load Balancing, and Replication

questions.text: What must be considered when using multiple hot standbys for read workloads? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: Automatic distribution of client connections requires external tools
Different standbys can be at different WAL positions
Reads from different nodes do not automatically form one consistent snapshot
Synchronous replication guarantees the same snapshot for every SELECT on all servers

questions.explanation: Physical replication provides readable copies, but balancing is handled externally and a consistent cross-server snapshot is not guaranteed.

source.locator: Read workload and consistency across nodes

questions.text: Which statements about cascading physical replication are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: A standby can receive WAL from another standby instead of directly from the primary
Cascading can reduce load and network traffic on the primary
The farther a node is down the chain, the greater its lag can be
The primary automatically waits for synchronous confirmation from every node in any cascade

questions.explanation: A cascade reduces load on the primary but adds potential lag; primary synchronization applies to directly connected synchronous standbys.

questions.text: What is an intentionally delayed physical standby used for?

answers.text: To provide a window for viewing and recovering the state before an erroneous data change
To allow writes on primary and standby at the same time
To replace WAL with logical SQL commands
To automatically synchronize DDL between different PostgreSQL versions

questions.explanation: Delayed WAL application creates a time window between primary and standby and can help recover from user error.

questions.text: Which statements about switching to a physical standby are correct? Select all correct answers.

answers.text: A planned switchover can be used for maintenance on the primary
Failover is required when the primary fails
Core PostgreSQL allows a standby to be promoted manually
Fully automatic failure detection and client reconfiguration appear automatically after streaming replication is enabled

questions.explanation: Streaming replication provides a standby that can be promoted, but automatic failover management requires additional cluster software and external client routing.
